summary: Batched embedding job split across regions causing mixed-rate billing on single invoice
description:
Issue summary:
Customer ran a single scheduled batched embedding job (batch_job_id: fjb-20260309-88) that was executed across two regions (us-west-2 and eu-west-1) due to autoscaling and regional overflow. The invoice shows the embeddings from that single logical job billed at two different per-embedding rates (higher eu rate and lower us rate) and assigned as separate line items rather than a single consolidated line with the applied enterprise committed rate.

Impact:
- Customer reports a $3,200 unexpected charge on the invoice for the billing period 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-10.
- Billing attributes ~1.1M embedding units to eu-west-1 at on-demand rate instead of the customer's committed enterprise rate for embeddings.
- Customer requests an adjustment or credit and explanation of why a single job was split for metering.

Environment:
- Account: acct-FA-0192 (enterprise, committed embedding tier activated 2026-02-01)
- Job: scheduled nightly batched embedding (internal job name: site-search-embed), batch_job_id: fjb-20260309-88
- Regions seen in logs: us-west-2 (primary), eu-west-1 (overflow)
- Model: text-embedding-3-large

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Triggered scheduled job on 2026-03-09 03:00 UTC.
2) Job enqueued 3.1M rows; runtime scheduler split into shards and distributed to available workers.
3) Customer observed shards being processed in us-west-2 until capacity threshold; remainder routed to eu-west-1.
4) After job completion, customer saw two invoice line items and higher-than-expected charge.

Observed behavior:
- Metering records show separate usage windows and region tags for shards.
- Billing connector applied region-specific on-demand tier pricing to eu-west usage and enterprise committed rate to us-west usage.
- Accounting treated eu-west shard usage as out-of-scope for enterprise commitment, causing discrepancy.

Expected behavior:
- A single logical job should be eligible for customer committed rates regardless of the region the individual worker executed in, if the account has an org-level embedding commitment that covers the total usage.

Logs / evidence:
- Customer provided job trace: fjb-20260309-88 (attached link to S3: s3://support-attachments/SUP-403217/fjb-20260309-88-trace.log )
- Metering export snippet (rows): "2026-03-09T03:12:17Z,acct-FA-0192,text-embedding-3-large,eu-west-1,shard-7,embeddings=550000"
- Invoice lines: INV-2026-03-10-FA0192 lines 4 and 7 reference embeddings EU and US rates.

Additional notes:
- Customer confirms they have an org-level committed embedding discount (contract ref: C-2026-E-77).
- Customer has strict finance cutoffs and asks for an interim credit while engineering investigates.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis: The metering pipeline emits per-shard region metadata at ingest. The billing join currently matches commitments against the region field before attempting an org-level commit mapping. In the case of overflowed shards, region != primary_region and the commitment id was not attached to the shard-level metering rows. Preliminary fix options: (1) backfill commitment_id into shard-level rows using parent job metadata, (2) change billing join order to prefer org-level commitment when present, (3) issue credits for affected invoice lines. Proved reproduction in staging by running a large batch job with forced overflow; observed same double-line behavior. Related PR to billing-join logic: PR#billing/1315 (under review).
resolution: Pending engineering patch to billing join logic. Provisional credit requested; finance assigned a hold request FIN-REQ-1229. If billing change lands and backfill confirms, customer will receive credit for the eu-west on-demand portion and invoice will be reissued. Follow-up: implement commit_id propagation at scheduler ingestion and add an automated test for cross-region batch jobs.
next_steps: 1) Billing Eng to merge PR#1315 and run backfill job (target 2026-03-16). 2) Finance to issue provisional credit of $3,200 upon confirmation of affected invoice lines. 3) Scheduler to add commit_id propagation to metering export. 4) Communicate timeline to customer and update ticket with credit memo ID.
